lines.en: Really? Is it picked by hand?

facts.label: Passivo no presente
facts.sub: Afirmativa: Coffee is grown in Brazil. Pergunta: Is it made here? Negativa: It isn’t made here. Use by só quando importa quem faz: It is baked by my sister.

facts.label: Passivo no presente
facts.sub: Use am/is/are + particípio para processos e fatos: Coffee is grown in Brazil. O foco é o produto ou o processo. Use is no singular e are no plural: The beans are roasted.

facts.label: Por quem
facts.sub: Quando importa quem faz, use by: The cake is baked by my sister. Quando não importa, o by some: The cake is baked here. Em explicações de processos, quase nunca se diz o agente.

compare.ask: This coffee is grown in Brazil.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “O café é cultivado aqui”, com ser + particípio, ou “cultivam café aqui”.
compare.tip: Diga: “This coffee is grown in Brazil.”
compare.us: Em inglês: am/is/are + particípio. Diga Coffee is grown in Brazil. Use are no plural: Beans are roasted.

group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The present passive is am/is/are + past participle.
We say “Coffee grows by farmers” for a process.
items.why: We say Coffee is grown by farmers.

items.s: “Cups are made of paper” is correct.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The present passive is am/is/are + past participle. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “Coffee grows by farmers” for a process. → Falso (We say Coffee is grown by farmers.)
“Cups are made of paper” is correct. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A small cafe · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy afternoon in Seattle. Abe works in a small cafe near the market. Big bags of coffee beans stand behind the counter. Eva comes in and shakes her umbrella. She wants something warm to drink. Abe smiles and starts to talk about his coffee.
“Welcome! This coffee is grown in Brazil and Colombia.” says Abe. “Really? Is it picked by hand?” says Eva. “Some of it is. Then it’s dried, roasted and sold all over the world.” says Abe.
